description: Built the Laravel backend of CheckProof's new Scheduling Tool, automating maintenance task scheduling, expiry deviations, and push alerts on a SaaS platform used in 35+ countries. metrics.label: database round trips per status change
to clear 1,000 healthy tasks queued behind 1M broken ones

decisions.title: Took the 1.69× speedup. Turned down the 4.4× one.
decisions.problem: Writes took most of each monitor run, so the write path decided how much work the monitor could handle.
decisions.rejected: A raw row writer, measured 4.4–4.9× faster
decisions.choice: Wrote each status change and its history row in one statement, so the two can't come apart. That cut 4 database round trips to 1.
decisions.tradeoff: Left the bigger speedup unused. The raw writer needed a second copy of the transition rules, and two copies drift apart. If one worker is not enough, the monitor can run once per status instead.
decisions.proof: Measured both writers on the same 1M-task backlog before choosing, then stress-tested the result: zero failures or deadlocks. The decision is on record with the condition that would reopen it.

decisions.title: One broken customer can't stall the rest
decisions.problem: A failed task stayed at the front of the queue and was retried on every run. One customer's bad data could hold up maintenance tasks for every other customer.
decisions.rejected: One failure limit for the whole run
decisions.choice: Gave each company a failure budget per run, and made a failed task wait longer after each failure, up to 60 minutes.
decisions.tradeoff: A broken backlog is held back, not cleared. It waits until its cause is fixed.
decisions.proof: In a test, 1M broken tasks from two companies sat at the front of the queue. The monitor tried 100 from each, set both companies aside, and cleared a third company's 1,000 healthy tasks in 3 seconds of a 50-second run. The old limit stopped the whole run after 100 failures, so those healthy tasks would have waited.

decisions.title: Left a known race in. On purpose.
decisions.problem: A user can complete a task while the monitor writes it, and the monitor's older write wins.
decisions.rejected: A status guard on every write
decisions.choice: Kept the write path as it is. The guard would add a cost to every status change to protect a rare one.
decisions.tradeoff: A rare overwrite is still possible until production shows it matters.
decisions.proof: Characterization tests pin the current behavior, so the race is a decision on record, not a bug waiting to be found.
